required_work: Carry the owner-qualified target binding on the upgrade-proposal envelope from canon into generated projections, fixtures, and admission checks.
objective: Canon now qualifies the upgrade-proposal envelope's target by owner reference rather than hard-requiring a system identifier, which is what lets a project-scoped maintenance profile exist without a fabricated System genesis. Nothing downstream of canon carries that yet: the generated projections, the positive and negative fixtures, and the admission checks still encode the older required-system shape. Bind the qualified target across the registry projections and admission path, and prove that an envelope naming a non-system owner is admitted for exactly the owners canon qualifies and refused for every other. UPGRADE_PROPOSAL_OWNER_QUALIFIED_TARGET_BINDING_EXIT=0.
falsifiable_claim: Canon's owner-qualified target binding is expressible end to end: the generated projections carry the qualified target, an envelope naming a qualified non-system owner is admitted, an envelope naming an unqualified owner is refused by name, and no path reintroduces a required system identifier.
selected_profile: The selected single-node deployment's improvement plane: the upgrade-proposal envelope, its registry projections, and the admission path that accepts or refuses one.

canon_snapshot.snapshot_role: Provenance for the canon revision this record was authored against. Drift detection is owned by generated/canon-baseline.v1.json via tools/canon-impact.mjs.

current_implementation_evidence: EXTRACTED OBLIGATION. This record exists because an external planning document held an active, unratified-into-the-estate obligation with no canonical record. Its canon half landed; its program half did not, and an obligation that lives only in a plan outside the estate is a competing guide. The plan was reclassified historical once this record was written; see _archive/manifests/external-plan-disposition.v1.json.
Verified at 7ee7acc2e: the canon owner carries the owner-qualified target binding, and no work-item record in the estate names it. The gap is the program half, not the canon half.
in_scope: Generated projections for the upgrade-proposal envelope updated to the owner-qualified target binding, derived from the contract registry rather than hand-edited.

Positive fixtures for every owner kind canon qualifies, and negative fixtures for an unqualified owner kind, a missing target binding, and a target whose admission domain does not match its owner kind.
The admission check that refuses an envelope whose target binding is absent or unqualified, refusing by a stable name that a test can assert and a record can cite.
A sweep of the three foundation owners canon named for residual assumptions that a target is always a system, recording any that cannot be removed as a named gap rather than silently leaving them.
out_of_scope: Changing what a system-scoped upgrade proposal means. System-scoped semantics are unchanged; this widens who may be named as a target, not what happens to a system.
Implementing project-scoped maintenance behaviour. This cut makes the target expressible; it activates no profile and grants no capability.
Any canon edit. The canon half of this obligation has landed and is not reopened here.
positive_proof: An envelope naming each owner kind canon qualifies is admitted, its projection round-trips through the registry-generated types, and the retained literal appears exactly once.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Predeclared refusals, each by name: an envelope with no target binding; an envelope naming an owner kind outside the qualified set; an envelope whose admission domain contradicts its owner kind; an envelope carrying both a legacy required system identifier and a qualified target, which must refuse rather than silently prefer one; a projection regenerated from a registry entry that still encodes the required-system shape, which must fail closed rather than emit a stale type.
The baseline is that no fixture, projection, or admission check exercises a non-system target today, so the qualified binding is unproven downstream of canon.

code_anchors.evidence_scope: the registry entry the projections and fixtures must be regenerated from; presence is not proof of this work item

remaining_nonclaims: Admitting a non-system target is not a claim that any project-scoped maintenance profile exists, is bounded, or is safe. It makes the target expressible and nothing else.
This record closes no stage, grants no capability, and publishes no claim.
Extraction from a plan is not ratification of that plan. Only this record's own proof closes this record.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if the qualified target cannot be admitted without reintroducing a required system identifier anywhere on the path, or if a projection can only be made to compile by hand-editing generated output. In either case the honest outcome is a named gap against the canon owner, never a hand-maintained projection or a fixture that pins the older shape.
exit_criteria: Projections, fixtures, and admission checks all carry the owner-qualified target binding; every predeclared refusal fires by name; no path requires a system identifier; and the retained literal appears exactly once.
